{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01WCjNyTBCaL6C2yFXCpiF3V","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# iKnowMed Generation 2 (Ontada / McKesson) — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: https://www.ontada.com/developer/\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→iKnowMed Generation 2 is a cloud-based, web-accessible electronic health record (EHR) system designed exclusively for oncology and hematology practices. It is a specialty EHR — not a general-purpose system — built specifically for the clinical workflows of community oncologists, including chemotherapy treatment planning, cancer staging, regimen management, and precision medicine. The product is developed and maintained by McKesson Specialty Health Technology Products LLC, operating under the Ontada brand.\n     9→\n    10→iKnowMed was originally developed in 1996 and acquired by US Oncology in 2004. McKesson Corporation acquired US Oncology Inc. in December 2010 for approximately $2.16 billion (including $1.6 billion in assumed debt), bringing iKnowMed into the McKesson portfolio. In May 2013, McKesson Specialty Health announced iKnowMed Generation 2, a next-generation rebuild developed in collaboration with over 200 practicing oncologists. In December 2020, McKesson launched Ontada as a dedicated oncology technology and insights business, and iKnowMed became a core component of the Ontada product suite. The name \"Ontada\" combines \"oncology\" and \"data,\" reflecting the business's dual focus on clinical care delivery and real-world data/research.\n    11→\n    12→Ontada is headquartered in Boston, MA (33 Arch Street, 20th Floor) and operates as a business unit within McKesson Corporation. The developer contact (Arun Meelyan, Arun.Meelyan@McKesson.com) reflects the McKesson organizational structure.\n    13→\n    14→## Product: iKnowMed Generation 2\n    15→\n    16→CHPL ID: 9580 (15.04.04.2920.iKno.30.01.1.180508)\n    17→\n    18→### What It Is\n    19→\n    20→iKnowMed Generation 2 Version 3 is a web-based, mobile-optimized oncology EHR certified under the ONC 2015 Edition criteria (certification date May 8, 2018, certified by Drummond Group Inc.). It is the only next-generation EHR designed exclusively for oncology and hematology available on the market. The system provides cloud-based access to patient charts, treatment decision support, and oncology-specific clinical workflows from any web browser, with an iOS mobile app for on-the-go access.\n    21→\n    22→The product is offered as a monthly subscription fee per user, covering access, maintenance, support, and upgrades. Additional costs include one-time professional services for implementation, setup, and user training, plus one-time setup fees and annual maintenance for interface configurations.\n    23→\n    24→The system depends on NewCropRx for e-prescribing functionality and Surescripts Clinical Messaging for secure direct messaging. Providers must register with Surescripts (DirectTrust network participant) to maintain these capabilities. Direct exchange messaging is not available outside the Surescripts/DirectTrust network.\n    25→\n    26→### Users & Market\n    27→\n    28→iKnowMed serves the community oncology market exclusively. Key metrics reported across sources (numbers vary by date and source):\n    29→\n    30→- **2,700+ oncology providers** actively use the platform (Ontada's most recent figures)\n    31→- **2,400 providers** within The US Oncology Network specifically (December 2024 data)\n    32→- **620+ sites of care** nationwide (at time of ONC certification)\n    33→- **1.5 million+ active patient portal users** nationally\n    34→- **1 million+ clinical decisions** supported through the platform\n    35→- **~2.5 million patient records** in the system\n    36→- **~1.4 million patients** seen annually across the connected network\n    37→\n    38→The US Oncology Network, one of the nation's largest integrated community oncology networks, is the primary user base. The network's affiliated practices use iKnowMed as their standard EHR. Ontada also connects to Onmark practices beyond the core network. US Oncology Network practices care for approximately one in five cancer patients in the United States.\n    39→\n    40→Intended users per ONC certification: Prescribers (oncologists/hematologists), Nurses, and Configuration Users (practice administrators). Day-to-day users include oncologists (treatment planning, charting, ordering), nurses (medication administration documentation, treatment monitoring), clinical staff (patient intake, documentation), and practice administrators (configuration, analytics).\n    41→\n    42→iKnowMed has been recognized as the top-ranked EHR platform for oncologists and hematologists for five consecutive years by Black Book Rankings. In KLAS Research's July 2025 oncology EHR ranking, iKnowMed scored 80.1 out of 100, placing second behind Epic Beacon (86.3) and ahead of Flatiron Health OncoEMR (79.8) and Elekta ONE (76.7).\n    43→\n    44→### Modules & Functionality\n    45→\n    46→Based on vendor website, McKesson product pages, mandatory disclosures, FHIR API documentation, and third-party reviews:\n    47→\n Ontada provides a data dictionary (b10_data_dictionary.xlsx) describing the contents of each exported table. The exact content varies by organization based on which iKnowMed features are active, configuration choices, clinical usage patterns, and available documentation.\n   193→\n   194→Beyond the standard clinical EHR data, iKnowMed's deep oncology focus means the system stores specialty-specific data not found in general EHRs:\n   195→- Cancer-specific diagnosis and staging information (tumor type, stage, grade)\n   196→- Chemotherapy regimen selections and treatment cycles\n   197→- Biomarker and molecular test orders and results\n   198→- NCCN pathway compliance tracking\n   199→- Drug toxicity monitoring data\n   200→- BSA (body surface area) calculations for dosing\n   201→- Treatment response assessments\n   202→\n   203→### Deployment & Architecture\n   204→\n   205→iKnowMed Generation 2 is a **cloud-based** system. It is accessed via web browser and does not require local software installation. The iOS mobile app provides additional access to patient charts and appointments. The system login URL (https://ikm.ontada.com/) confirms the cloud-hosted deployment model under the Ontada domain.\n   206→\n   207→The system is ISO 9001:2015 Stage 2 certified, HIPAA compliant, and ICD-10 certified.\n   208→\n   209→### Integrations\n   210→\n   211→- **Surescripts/DirectTrust** — e-prescribing and direct messaging (required dependency)\n   212→- **NewCropRx** — e-prescribing engine (required dependency)\n   213→- **NCCN** — Value Pathways and Clinical Practice Guidelines integration\n   214→- **Ontada Marketplace** — third-party developer ecosystem via Certified API and Value Add Developer Programs\n   215→- **FHIR R4 API** — standards-based integration for external applications\n   216→- **Immunization registries** — public health reporting\n   217→- **Cancer registries** — case reporting\n   218→\n   219→**Known integration challenges**: KLAS user reviews note persistent interoperability concerns, with nearly half of respondents reporting poor integration with external EHRs, labs, and scheduling tools. One user described interfacing with iKnowMed as \"a nightmare.\" This likely reflects iKnowMed's position as a specialty system that must coexist alongside hospital/health system general-purpose EHRs.\n   220→\n   221→### Ecosystem & Beyond-EHR Capabilities\n   222→\n   223→iKnowMed is not just a clinical EHR — it serves as the data collection backbone for Ontada's broader oncology intelligence platform:\n   224→\n   225→**Real-World Data & Research**\n   226→- iKnowMed data feeds Ontada's real-world evidence (RWE) generation engine\n   227→- Over 400 real-world research publications supported by Ontada\n   228→- Data from ~2.5 million patient records used for research insights\n   229→- FDA selected Ontada to investigate rare cancer natural history\n   230→- Partnerships with pharmaceutical companies (Merck, BeiGene, Amgen) for evidence-based research\n   231→\n   232→**AI & Advanced Analytics**\n   233→- ON.Genuity platform leveraging AI for oncology data analysis\n   234→- 2024 collaboration with Microsoft to transform unstructured oncology data using Azure OpenAI technology\n   235→- Genospace for next-generation sequencing (genomic) data analysis\n   236→\n   237→**Data Products (for life sciences companies)**\n   238→- ON.ClinicalDataView — clinical data access\n   239→- ON.Insights — oncology market insights\n   240→- ON.OutcomesView — health economics and outcomes research\n   241→- ON.JourneyView — patient journey analytics\n   242→- Alerts — real-time notification system\n   243→\n   244→**Provider Education**\n   245→- Ontada Learn — digital education platform for oncology practitioners\n   246→- Practice-based education and strategy effectiveness training\n   247→\n   248→## Competitive Landscape\n   249→\n   250→iKnowMed competes primarily with:\n   251→1. **Epic Beacon** — Epic's oncology module, which leads KLAS rankings (86.3 vs iKnowMed's 80.1) and dominates in health system/academic oncology settings\n   252→2. **Flatiron Health OncoEMR** — another oncology-specific EHR focused on community oncology and real-world data, scoring 79.8 in KLAS\n   253→3. **Elekta ONE (Mosaiq)** — primarily radiation oncology information system, scoring 76.7 in KLAS\n   254→\n   255→iKnowMed's primary differentiation is its deep integration with The US Oncology Network (the largest community oncology network) and its dual role as both a clinical EHR and a data collection platform for real-world oncology research. While Epic Beacon leads in overall satisfaction, iKnowMed's oncology-specific design (built by oncologists for oncologists) gives it advantages in community oncology workflows that general-purpose EHRs with oncology modules cannot easily replicate.\n   256→\n   257→## Research Notes\n   258→\n   259→- iKnowMed is tightly coupled with the US Oncology Network; its market penetration outside that network appears limited, though the Ontada Marketplace and developer programs suggest efforts to broaden the ecosystem.\n   260→- The dual role of iKnowMed as both clinical EHR and real-world data collection instrument for pharmaceutical research is distinctive. Clinician data entry directly feeds Ontada's commercial data products.\n   261→- The EHI export uses pipe-delimited flat files rather than standard formats like FHIR bundles — the data dictionary (b10_data_dictionary.xlsx) would need to be reviewed in Phase 2 to understand the full export schema.\n   262→- The 2018 certification date is notably old; many competing products have more recent certifications. However, the FHIR API and EHI export capabilities appear to be actively maintained.\n   263→- Interoperability with non-Ontada systems is a documented pain point per KLAS reviews, which is significant for practices that need iKnowMed to coexist with hospital EHRs.\n   264→- Full source list available in sources.json.\n   265→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. It is a specialty EHR — not a general-purpose system — built specifically for the clinical workflows of community oncologists, including chemotherapy treatment planning, cancer staging, regimen management, and precision medicine. The product is developed and maintained by McKesson Specialty Health Technology Products LLC, operating under the Ontada brand.\n\niKnowMed was originally developed in 1996 and acquired by US Oncology in 2004. McKesson Corporation acquired US Oncology Inc. in December 2010 for approximately $2.16 billion (including $1.6 billion in assumed debt), bringing iKnowMed into the McKesson portfolio. In May 2013, McKesson Specialty Health announced iKnowMed Generation 2, a next-generation rebuild developed in collaboration with over 200 practicing oncologists. In December 2020, McKesson launched Ontada as a dedicated oncology technology and insights business, and iKnowMed became a core component of the Ontada product suite. The name \"Ontada\" combines \"oncology\" and \"data,\" reflecting the business's dual focus on clinical care delivery and real-world data/research.\n\nOntada is headquartered in Boston, MA (33 Arch Street, 20th Floor) and operates as a business unit within McKesson Corporation. The developer contact (Arun Meelyan, Arun.Meelyan@McKesson.com) reflects the McKesson organizational structure.\n\n## Product: iKnowMed Generation 2\n\nCHPL ID: 9580 (15.04.04.2920.iKno.30.01.1.180508)\n\n### What It Is\n\niKnowMed Generation 2 Version 3 is a web-based, mobile-optimized oncology EHR certified under the ONC 2015 Edition criteria (certification date May 8, 2018, certified by Drummond Group Inc.). It is the only next-generation EHR designed exclusively for oncology and hematology available on the market. The system provides cloud-based access to patient charts, treatment decision support, and oncology-specific clinical workflows from any web browser, with an iOS mobile app for on-the-go access.\n\nThe product is offered as a monthly subscription fee per user, covering access, maintenance, support, and upgrades. Additional costs include one-time professional services for implementation, setup, and user training, plus one-time setup fees and annual maintenance for interface configurations.\n\nThe system depends on NewCropRx for e-prescribing functionality and Surescripts Clinical Messaging for secure direct messaging. Providers must register with Surescripts (DirectTrust network participant) to maintain these capabilities. Direct exchange messaging is not available outside the Surescripts/DirectTrust network.\n\n### Users & Market\n\niKnowMed serves the community oncology market exclusively. Key metrics reported across sources (numbers vary by date and source):\n\n- **2,700+ oncology providers** actively use the platform (Ontada's most recent figures)\n- **2,400 providers** within The US Oncology Network specifically (December 2024 data)\n- **620+ sites of care** nationwide (at time of ONC certification)\n- **1.5 million+ active patient portal users** nationally\n- **1 million+ clinical decisions** supported through the platform\n- **~2.5 million patient records** in the system\n- **~1.4 million patients** seen annually across the connected network\n\nThe US Oncology Network, one of the nation's largest integrated community oncology networks, is the primary user base. The network's affiliated practices use iKnowMed as their standard EHR. Ontada also connects to Onmark practices beyond the core network. US Oncology Network practices care for approximately one in five cancer patients in the United States.\n\nIntended users per ONC certification: Prescribers (oncologists/hematologists), Nurses, and Configuration Users (practice administrators). Day-to-day users include oncologists (treatment planning, charting, ordering), nurses (medication administration documentation, treatment monitoring), clinical staff (patient intake, documentation), and practice administrators (configuration, analytics).\n\niKnowMed has been recognized as the top-ranked EHR platform for oncologists and hematologists for five consecutive years by Black Book Rankings. In KLAS Research's July 2025 oncology EHR ranking, iKnowMed scored 80.1 out of 100, placing second behind Epic Beacon (86.3) and ahead of Flatiron Health OncoEMR (79.8) and Elekta ONE (76.7).\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on vendor website, McKesson product pages, mandatory disclosures, FHIR API documentation, and third-party reviews:\n\n**Oncology-Specific Clinical Documentation**\n- Cancer diagnosis and staging using AJCC (American Joint Committee on Cancer) and FIGO (International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics) staging criteria\n- Comprehensive patient charting with oncology-focused templates and customizable dashboards\n- Flexible documentation options with auto-sharing of clinical notes\n- Encounter-based documentation with customizable charts and order sets\n- Elimination of handwritten notes and drug orders to minimize inaccuracies\n\n**Chemotherapy Treatment Planning & Regimen Management**\n- Extensive, up-to-date cancer regimen library organized by disease categories and treatment types\n- Value Pathways powered by NCCN and NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) integrated directly into clinical workflow\n- Personalized protocol creation for disease complications, patient-specific needs, and drug replacements\n- Pre-populated order forms with ability to save drafts and access completed forms in patient chart\n- Safety alerts for medication conflicts and high toxicity levels\n\n**Clinical Decision Support (Clear Value Plus)**\n- Clear Value Plus is a companion clinical decision support tool highlighting evidence-based treatment options\n- Integrated financial information alongside clinical pathways at point of care\n- Real-time reporting and benchmarking against evidence-based standards\n- Constantly refreshed clinical information including guidelines and pathways\n\n**Precision Medicine & Biomarker Support**\n- Biomarker ordering within the EHR displaying latest targeted therapy options at point-of-need\n- Biomarker test guidelines suggesting molecular tests by disease type\n- Rapid integration of new guidelines and biomarkers as they emerge\n- Real-time data capture enhancing precision medicine decision-making\n- Ontada's Precision Care Companion (announced 2024) for community oncology precision medicine workflows\n\n**Clinical Decision Support Alerts**\n- Drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction alerts\n- Clinical decision support monitoring changes in BSA, lab results, hepatic/renal dysfunction\n- Actionable alerts allowing single-click implementation of recommended changes\n- Safety alerts for toxicity levels and medication conflicts\n\n**Electronic Prescribing**\n- Surescripts-certified e-prescribing\n- Electronic prescription exchange with pharmacies on the Surescripts network\n- Real-time patient eligibility and formulary information\n- Prescription history access\n- Integration via NewCropRx\n\n**Practice Analytics (Practice Insights)**\n- Multi-source data aggregation for clinical, operational, and financial insights\n- Drug utilization metrics and clinical pathway compliance based on NCCN Guidelines\n- Peer and industry benchmarking\n- Quality initiative tracking for value-based care programs (MIPS, Oncology Care Model)\n- Performance metrics and productivity measures\n- Proactive, actionable insights for oncology practice management\n\n**Patient Engagement (Ontada Health)**\n- Secure patient portal providing online access to clinical information\n- Provider-patient communication tools and secure messaging\n- Expanded library of patient education resources\n- Interoperable technology for sharing information across care systems\n- 1.5 million+ active patient portal users nationally\n\n**Appointment & Scheduling Management**\n- Appointment management integrated into the EHR\n- Mobile access to patient appointments via iOS app\n\n**Billing & Charge Capture**\n- Automated charge capture functionality\n- EM coding support\n- Integration with revenue cycle management workflows\n\n**Quality Reporting**\n- CMS-approved Qualified Clinical Data Registry (QCDR) for MIPS quality measure reporting\n- iKnowMed users can submit quality data directly to CMS (2023 QCDR designation)\n- Clinical quality measure CMS68v6 certified\n\n**Public Health Reporting**\n- Immunization registry reporting (certified under 170.315(f)(1))\n- Electronic case reporting (certified under 170.315(f)(2))\n- Cancer case reporting (certified under 170.315(f)(5))\n\n**Interoperability & APIs**\n- FHIR R4 API (Ontada FHIR Server) with 30+ clinical resources\n- SMART on FHIR support for EHR-embedded application launches\n- Client Credentials authentication for backend integration\n- OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect for authorization\n- Transitions of care via C-CDA (certified (b)(1)-(b)(3))\n- EHI bulk export via FHIR Group resource (certified (b)(10))\n- Certified API Developer Program (self-serve) and Value Add Developer Program (by-invitation with sandbox, marketplace listing, workflow integration)\n- Ontada Marketplace for third-party application distribution\n\n**Mobile Access**\n- iOS app providing secure cloud-based access to patient charts and appointments\n- Web-based mobile-optimized interface accessible from any device\n\n**Document Management**\n- Document storage and management within patient records\n- Clinical note auto-sharing across care team\n\n### Data & Content\n\nThe FHIR API documentation reveals 30+ clinical data resource types accessible through the Ontada FHIR Server, providing a comprehensive view of the data model:\n\n**Patient Identity & Demographics**\n- Patient demographics, contact information, identifiers\n- Related persons (family members, caregivers)\n- Coverage (insurance information)\n\n**Clinical Encounters & Care Coordination**\n- Encounter records\n- Appointment scheduling data\n- CarePlan (treatment plans)\n- CareTeam assignments\n- Goal tracking\n- ServiceRequest (orders and referrals)\n\n**Diagnoses & Conditions**\n- Condition records (cancer diagnoses, staging, comorbidities)\n- Cancer staging data (AJCC, FIGO criteria)\n\n**Medications & Prescriptions**\n- MedicationRequest (prescriptions and orders)\n- MedicationStatement (reported medications)\n- MedicationAdministration (infusion/treatment administration records)\n- MedicationDispense (dispensing records)\n- Medication reference data\n\n**Laboratory & Observations**\n- Observation (lab results, vital signs, clinical measurements including BSA)\n- DiagnosticReport (lab reports, pathology reports)\n- Specimen data\n\n**Treatment & Procedures**\n- Procedure records (chemotherapy administration, surgeries, biopsies)\n- Chemotherapy regimen data (based on NCCN pathways)\n- Treatment protocol documentation\n\n**Safety Data**\n- AllergyIntolerance records\n- Immunization records\n\n**Documents & Provenance**\n- DocumentReference (clinical documents, notes)\n- Binary (document content)\n- Provenance (data source tracking)\n- QuestionnaireResponse (patient-reported data)\n\n**Administrative & Reference**\n- Organization, Practitioner, Location, Device reference data\n- Provider profiles and facility information\n\nThe EHI export functionality delivers data as compressed zip files containing pipe-delimited (|) flat files. Ontada provides a data dictionary (b10_data_dictionary.xlsx) describing the contents of each exported table. The exact content varies by organization based on which iKnowMed features are active, configuration choices, clinical usage patterns, and available documentation.\n\nBeyond the standard clinical EHR data, iKnowMed's deep oncology focus means the system stores specialty-specific data not found in general EHRs:\n- Cancer-specific diagnosis and staging information (tumor type, stage, grade)\n- Chemotherapy regimen selections and treatment cycles\n- Biomarker and molecular test orders and results\n- NCCN pathway compliance tracking\n- Drug toxicity monitoring data\n- BSA (body surface area) calculations for dosing\n- Treatment response assessments\n\n### Deployment & Architecture\n\niKnowMed Generation 2 is a **cloud-based** system. It is accessed via web browser and does not require local software installation. The iOS mobile app provides additional access to patient charts and appointments. The system login URL (https://ikm.ontada.com/) confirms the cloud-hosted deployment model under the Ontada domain.\n\nThe system is ISO 9001:2015 Stage 2 certified, HIPAA compliant, and ICD-10 certified.\n\n### Integrations\n\n- **Surescripts/DirectTrust** — e-prescribing and direct messaging (required dependency)\n- **NewCropRx** — e-prescribing engine (required dependency)\n- **NCCN** — Value Pathways and Clinical Practice Guidelines integration\n- **Ontada Marketplace** — third-party developer ecosystem via Certified API and Value Add Developer Programs\n- **FHIR R4 API** — standards-based integration for external applications\n- **Immunization registries** — public health reporting\n- **Cancer registries** — case reporting\n\n**Known integration challenges**: KLAS user reviews note persistent interoperability concerns, with nearly half of respondents reporting poor integration with external EHRs, labs, and scheduling tools. One user described interfacing with iKnowMed as \"a nightmare.\" This likely reflects iKnowMed's position as a specialty system that must coexist alongside hospital/health system general-purpose EHRs.\n\n### Ecosystem & Beyond-EHR Capabilities\n\niKnowMed is not just a clinical EHR — it serves as the data collection backbone for Ontada's broader oncology intelligence platform:\n\n**Real-World Data & Research**\n- iKnowMed data feeds Ontada's real-world evidence (RWE) generation engine\n- Over 400 real-world research publications supported by Ontada\n- Data from ~2.5 million patient records used for research insights\n- FDA selected Ontada to investigate rare cancer natural history\n- Partnerships with pharmaceutical companies (Merck, BeiGene, Amgen) for evidence-based research\n\n**AI & Advanced Analytics**\n- ON.Genuity platform leveraging AI for oncology data analysis\n- 2024 collaboration with Microsoft to transform unstructured oncology data using Azure OpenAI technology\n- Genospace for next-generation sequencing (genomic) data analysis\n\n**Data Products (for life sciences companies)**\n- ON.ClinicalDataView — clinical data access\n- ON.Insights — oncology market insights\n- ON.OutcomesView — health economics and outcomes research\n- ON.JourneyView — patient journey analytics\n- Alerts — real-time notification system\n\n**Provider Education**\n- Ontada Learn — digital education platform for oncology practitioners\n- Practice-based education and strategy effectiveness training\n\n## Competitive Landscape\n\niKnowMed competes primarily with:\n1. **Epic Beacon** — Epic's oncology module, which leads KLAS rankings (86.3 vs iKnowMed's 80.1) and dominates in health system/academic oncology settings\n2. **Flatiron Health OncoEMR** — another oncology-specific EHR focused on community oncology and real-world data, scoring 79.8 in KLAS\n3. **Elekta ONE (Mosaiq)** — primarily radiation oncology information system, scoring 76.7 in KLAS\n\niKnowMed's primary differentiation is its deep integration with The US Oncology Network (the largest community oncology network) and its dual role as both a clinical EHR and a data collection platform for real-world oncology research. While Epic Beacon leads in overall satisfaction, iKnowMed's oncology-specific design (built by oncologists for oncologists) gives it advantages in community oncology workflows that general-purpose EHRs with oncology modules cannot easily replicate.\n\n## Research Notes\n\n- iKnowMed is tightly coupled with the US Oncology Network; its market penetration outside that network appears limited, though the Ontada Marketplace and developer programs suggest efforts to broaden the ecosystem.\n- The dual role of iKnowMed as both clinical EHR and real-world data collection instrument for pharmaceutical research is distinctive. Clinician data entry directly feeds Ontada's commercial data products.\n- The EHI export uses pipe-delimited flat files rather than standard formats like FHIR bundles — the data dictionary (b10_data_dictionary.xlsx) would need to be reviewed in Phase 2 to understand the full export schema.\n- The 2018 certification date is notably old; many competing products have more recent certifications. However, the FHIR API and EHI export capabilities appear to be actively maintained.\n- Interoperability with non-Ontada systems is a documented pain point per KLAS reviews, which is significant for practices that need iKnowMed to coexist with hospital EHRs.\n- Full source list available in sources.json.\n","numLines":265,"startLine":1,"totalLines":265}}}

Part of McKesson Corporation, Ontada was founded on the core belief that precise insights &mdash; delivered exactly at the point of need &mdash; can save more patients&rsquo; lives. * Extracts the b10_data_dictionary.xlsx into structured JSON files.\n *\n * Usage: bun run extract-data-dictionary.ts\n *\n * Input:  ../b10_data_dictionary.xlsx\n * Output: data-dictionary.json          — full structured extraction\n *         summary.json                  — coverage/accounting stats\n */\n\nimport * as XLSX from \"xlsx\";\nimport { writeFileSync } from \"fs\";\nimport { join, dirname } from \"path\";\n\nconst scriptDir = dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname);\nconst inputPath = join(scriptDir, \"..\", \"b10_data_dictionary.xlsx\");\nconst outputDir = scriptDir;\n\ninterface Column {\n  column_name: string;\n  data_type: string;\n  data_length: number | null;\n  data_precision: number | null;\n  data_scale: number | null;\n  char_used: string | null;\n  column_desc: string | null;\n}\n\ninterface Table {\n  table_name: string;\n  table_desc: string | null;\n  source_sheet: string;\n  columns: Column[];\n}\n\ninterface OntadaHealthField {\n  field_name: string;\n  data_type: string;\n  description: string | null;\n  notes: string | null;\n}\n\ninterface OntadaHealthCollection {\n  collection_name: string;\n  source_sheet: string;\n  fields: OntadaHealthField[];\n}\n\ninterface DataDictionary {\n  extraction_date: string;\n  source_file: string;\n  sheets: string[];\n  tables: Table[];\n  ontada_health_collections: OntadaHealthCollection[];\n  stats: {\n    total_sheets: number;\n    total_tables: number;\n    total_columns: number;\n    tables_by_sheet: Record<string, number>;\n    columns_by_sheet: Record<string, number>;\n  };\n}\n\n// Read workbook\nconst wb = XLSX.readFile(inputPath);\nconsole.log(`Loaded workbook with sheets: ${wb.SheetNames.join(\", \")}`);\n\nconst tables: Table[] = [];\nconst ontadaCollections: OntadaHealthCollection[] = [];\nconst tablesBySheet: Record<string, number> = {};\nconst columnsBySheet: Record<string, number> = {};\nlet totalColumns = 0;\n\n// --- Sheet 1: iKnowMed ---\n{\n  const ws = wb.Sheets[\"iKnowMed\"];\n  const rows: any[] = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(ws);\n  const byTable = new Map<string, { desc: string | null; cols: Column[] }>();\n\n  for (const row of rows) {\n    const tableName = String(row.TABLE_NAME || \"\").trim();\n    if (!tableName) continue;\n\n    if (!byTable.has(tableName)) {\n      byTable.set(tableName, {\n        desc: row.TABLE_DESC ? String(row.TABLE_DESC).trim() : null,\n        cols: [],\n      });\n    }\n\n    byTable.get(tableName)!.cols.push({\n      column_name: String(row.COLUMN_NAME || \"\").trim(),\n      data_type: String(row.DATA_TYPE || \"\").trim(),\n      data_length: row.DATA_LENGTH != null ? Number(row.DATA_LENGTH) : null,\n      data_precision: null,\n      data_scale: null,\n      char_used: null,\n      column_desc: row.COLUMN_DESC ? String(row.COLUMN_DESC).trim() : null,\n    });\n  }\n\n  for (const [tableName, { desc, cols }] of byTable) {\n    tables.push({\n      table_name: tableName,\n      table_desc: desc,\n      source_sheet: \"iKnowMed\",\n      columns: cols,\n    });\n  }\n\n  tablesBySheet[\"iKnowMed\"] = byTable.size;\n  columnsBySheet[\"iKnowMed\"] = rows.length;\n  totalColumns += rows.length;\n  console.log(`  iKnowMed: ${byTable.size} tables, ${rows.length} columns`);\n}\n\n// --- Sheet 2: VBC ---\n{\n  const ws = wb.Sheets[\"VBC\"];\n  const rows: any[] = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(ws);\n  const byTable = new Map<string, Column[]>();\n\n  for (const row of rows) {\n    const tableName = String(row.table_name || \"\").trim();\n    if (!tableName) continue;\n\n    if (!byTable.has(tableName)) {\n      byTable.set(tableName, []);\n    }\n\n    byTable.get(tableName)!.push({\n      column_name: String(row.column_name || \"\").trim(),\n      data_type: String(row.data_type || \"\").trim(),\n      data_length: null,\n      data_precision: null,\n      data_scale: null,\n      char_used: null,\n      column_desc: null,\n    });\n  }\n\n  for (const [tableName, cols] of byTable) {\n    tables.push({\n      table_name: tableName,\n      table_desc: null,\n      source_sheet: \"VBC\",\n      columns: cols,\n    });\n  }\n\n  tablesBySheet[\"VBC\"] = byTable.size;\n  columnsBySheet[\"VBC\"] = rows.length;\n  totalColumns += rows.length;\n  console.log(`  VBC: ${byTable.size} tables, ${rows.length} columns`);\n}\n\n// --- Sheet 3: Patient History ---\n{\n  const ws = wb.Sheets[\"Patient History\"];\n  const rows: any[] = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(ws);\n  const byTable = new Map<string, Column[]>();\n\n  for (const row of rows) {\n    const tableName = String(row.TABLE_NAME || \"\").trim();\n    if (!tableName) continue;\n\n    if (!byTable.has(tableName)) {\n      byTable.set(tableName, []);\n    }\n\n    byTable.get(tableName)!.push({\n      column_name: String(row.COLUMN_NAME || \"\").trim(),\n      data_type: String(row.DATA_TYPE || \"\").trim(),\n      data_length: row.DATA_LENGTH != null ? Number(row.DATA_LENGTH) : null,\n      data_precision: row.DATA_PRECISION != null ? Number(row.DATA_PRECISION) : null,\n      data_scale: row.DATA_SCALE != null ? Number(row.DATA_SCALE) : null,\n      char_used: row.CHAR_USED ? String(row.CHAR_USED).trim() : null,\n      column_desc: null,\n    });\n  }\n\n  for (const [tableName, cols] of byTable) {\n    tables.push({\n      table_name: tableName,\n      table_desc: null,\n      source_sheet: \"Patient History\",\n      columns: cols,\n    });\n  }\n\n  tablesBySheet[\"Patient History\"] = byTable.size;\n  columnsBySheet[\"Patient History\"] = rows.length;\n  totalColumns += rows.length;\n  console.log(`  Patient History: ${byTable.size} tables, ${rows.length} columns`);\n}\n\n// --- Sheet 4: Ontada Health ---\n{\n  const ws = wb.Sheets[\"Ontada Health\"];\n  const rows: any[] = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json(ws);\n  const byCollection = new Map<string, OntadaHealthField[]>();\n\n  for (const row of rows) {\n    const collName = String(row.Collection || \"\").trim();\n    if (!collName) continue;\n\n    if (!byCollection.has(collName)) {\n      byCollection.set(collName, []);\n    }\n\n    byCollection.get(collName)!.push({\n      field_name: String(row[\"Field Name\"] || \"\").trim(),\n      data_type: String(row[\"Data Type\"] || \"\").trim(),\n      description: row.Description ? String(row.Description).trim() : null,\n      notes: row.Notes ? String(row.Notes).trim() : null,\n    });\n  }\n\n  for (const [collName, fields] of byCollection) {\n    ontadaCollections.push({\n      collection_name: collName,\n      source_sheet: \"Ontada Health\",\n      fields,\n    });\n  }\n\n  tablesBySheet[\"Ontada Health\"] = byCollection.size;\n  columnsBySheet[\"Ontada Health\"] = rows.length;\n  totalColumns += rows.length;\n  console.log(`  Ontada Health: ${byCollection.size} collections, ${rows.length} fields`);\n}\n\nconst totalTables = tables.length + ontadaCollections.length;\n\nconst dataDictionary: DataDictionary = {\n  extraction_date: new Date().toISOString().split(\"T\")[0],\n  source_file: \"b10_data_dictionary.xlsx\",\n  sheets: wb.SheetNames,\n  tables,\n  ontada_health_collections: ontadaCollections,\n  stats: {\n    total_sheets: wb.SheetNames.length,\n    total_tables: totalTables,\n    total_columns: totalColumns,\n    tables_by_sheet: tablesBySheet,\n    columns_by_sheet: columnsBySheet,\n  },\n};\n\n// Write full data dictionary\nconst ddPath = join(outputDir, \"data-dictionary.json\");\nwriteFileSync(ddPath, JSON.stringify(dataDictionary, null, 2));\nconsole.log(`\\nWrote ${ddPath}`);\n\n// Write summary\nconst summary = {\n  extraction_date: dataDictionary.extraction_date,\n  source_file: dataDictionary.source_file,\n  total_sheets: dataDictionary.stats.total_sheets,\n  total_tables: dataDictionary.stats.total_tables,\n  total_columns: dataDictionary.stats.total_columns,\n  tables_by_sheet: dataDictionary.stats.tables_by_sheet,\n  columns_by_sheet: dataDictionary.stats.columns_by_sheet,\n  parse_failures: [],\n  table_list: tables.map((t) => ({\n    name: t.table_name,\n    sheet: t.source_sheet,\n    column_count: t.columns.length,\n    desc: t.table_desc,\n  })),\n  ontada_health_collection_list: ontadaCollections.map((c) => ({\n    name: c.collection_name,\n    sheet: c.source_sheet,\n    field_count: c.fields.length,\n  })),\n};\n\nconst summaryPath = join(outputDir, \"summary.json\");\nwriteFileSync(summaryPath, JSON.stringify(summary, null, 2));\nconsole.log(`Wrote ${summaryPath}`);\n\nconsole.log(`\\nDone. total.`);\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":150,"cache_read_input_tokens":54230,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":150},"output_tokens":25,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"bf663c9b-80e5-4ddc-b9b4-2d3543e1f5f6","uuid":"c6c4de40-7f13-4f81-bf37-34913ad96cb1"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01FeuLpqVH5JGrbofbYchiGL","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01AA4qVLnVNoznmYbEh8hVx4","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/mckesson-specialty-health-technology-products-llc-ontada--iknowmed-generation-2/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# McKesson Specialty Health Technology Products LLC (Ontada) — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://www.ontada.com/Providers-Solutions/EHI/\n- Final URL (after redirect): https://www.ontada.com/point-of-care-solutions/ehi/\n- CHPL ID: 9580 (15.04.04.2920.iKno.30.01.1.180508)\n- Product: iKnowMed Generation 2, Version 3\n- Certification date: 2018-05-08\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Initial probe** — HTTP HEAD with curl:\n   ```\n   curl -sI -L \"https://www.ontada.com/Providers-Solutions/EHI/\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n   ```\n   Result: 301 redirect from `/Providers-Solutions/EHI/` to `/point-of-care-solutions/ehi/`, then 200 OK with `text/html` content type. Site is behind Cloudflare and Imperva CDN.\n\n2. **Fetched the page** — 72KB HTML page titled \"iKnowMed® EHI Export Capabilities\". The page is a simple single-page document (not an SPA) with:\n   - A brief description of the EHI export format\n   - A link to the (b)(10) Data Dictionary (XLSX)\n   - A list of factors that affect export content variability\n   - No additional sub-pages, accordions, or hidden sections\n\n3. **Found downloadable file** — searched HTML for file links:\n   ```\n   grep -oiE 'href=\"[^\"]*\\.(pdf|zip|xlsx|xls|csv|json)' page.html\n   ```\n   Found one file: `/siteassets/documents/b10_data_dictionary.xlsx`\n\n4. **Downloaded the data dictionary**:\n   ```\n   curl -sL \"https://www.ontada.com/siteassets/documents/b10_data_dictionary.xlsx\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o b10_data_dictionary.xlsx\n   ```\n   Confirmed: `file` reports \"Microsoft Excel 2007+\", 240KB.\n\n5. **Took a full-page screenshot** of the EHI page in Chrome for visual documentation.\n\n6. **No additional documentation found.** The page contains only the description and the single data dictionary download. There are no links to export format specifications, API docs, sample data, schema files, or user guides beyond what is on the page. The two external links on the page (to healthit.gov and the ONC certification criteria) are standard regulatory references, not vendor-specific documentation.\n\n## What Was Found\n\n### Export Format\n\nThe EHI export from iKnowMed Generation 2 produces a **ZIP file containing pipe-delimited (|) flat files** — one file per table/entity in the export. This is a proprietary database dump format, not a standard like FHIR or C-CDA. The page explicitly states this satisfies §170.315(b)(10).\n\nThe page notes that export content varies by organization based on:\n- Which iKnowMed features are in use\n- Configuration decisions made by the healthcare organization\n- The organization's clinical utilization of iKnowMed\n- The documentation in place at the healthcare organization\n\n### Data Dictionary (b10_data_dictionary.xlsx)\n\nThe data dictionary is a substantial Excel workbook with **4 sheets, 249 entities, and 5,679 field definitions**:\n\n**Sheet 1: iKnowMed** — 236 tables, 5,275 columns. This is the core EHR database schema and constitutes the vast majority of the export. Each row provides: TABLE_NAME, COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE, DATA_LENGTH, TABLE_DESC, and COLUMN_DESC. The descriptions are brief (typically just the Java class name) but present for most tables. Column descriptions are more substantive, often including the Java field type and optional/required annotations.\n\nKey table groups in the iKnowMed sheet:\n- **Patient demographics**: PATIENT (57 cols), PATIENT_CONTACT, PATIENT_IDENTIFICATION, PAT_RACE, PAT_ETHNICITY, PAT_LANGUAGE, PAT_GENDER_IDENTITY\n- **Clinical problems & diagnoses**: PAT_PROBLEM (36 cols), PAT_PROBLEM_INFERENCE, PROBLEM_DEF, BILLING_DIAG_DEF\n- **Medications & prescribing**: MEDICATION (53 cols), PATIENT_MEDICATION, PRESCRIPTION (35 cols), MEDICATION_PREFERENCE (92 cols), DISPENSABLE (35 cols), NEWDRUGRXTEMPLATE, RXRENEWALREQUEST, RX_CHANGE_REQUEST, RX_FILL_NOTIFICATION\n- **Orders & administration**: PAT_ORDER (182 cols — the largest table), PAT_ORDER_DOSE (75 cols), PAT_ORDER_ADMINISTRATION, PAT_ORDER_SESSION, PAT_ORDER_GROUP, PAT_ORDER_DISCONTINUATION, PAT_ORDER_INFERENCE\n- **Treatment regimens (oncology-specific)**: PAT_REGIMEN (99 cols), PAT_REGIMEN_CYCLE_DAYS, PAT_REGIMEN_INFERENCE, PAT_REGIMEN_SEQUENCE, PAT_REGIMEN_TREATMENT_GROUP, REGIMEN_DEF (41 cols), PAT_CHEMO_TREATMENT (34 cols), DATE_CYCLE_DAY, CYCLE_DAY_DELAY, CYCLE_DAY_MOVE\n- **Other oncology treatments**: PATIENT_RADIATION_TREATMENT (29 cols), PATIENT_SURGERY_TREATMENT, PAT_HOSPITAL_TREATMENT, PAT_OTHER_TREATMENT, PAT_PROCEDURE_TREATMENT, PAT_TRANSFUSN_TREATMENT, PAT_TREATMENT (49 cols), PAT_TREATMENT_HISTORY (54 cols)\n- **Lab results**: PAT_RESULT_HEADER (53 cols), PAT_RESULT_VALUE (41 cols), PAT_RESULT_ATTACHMENT, LAB_ANALYTE_DEF, LAB_PANEL_DEF, EXTERNAL_RESULT_PANEL_DEF, EXTERNAL_RESULT_VALUE_DEF\n- **Vitals & observations**: DAILY_VITALS, BASELINE_VITAL (28 cols), TREATMENT_VITAL (22 cols), TREATMENT_VITAL_SET, PAT_PERFORMANCE_STATUS, PATIENT_SMOKING_STATUS\n- **Allergies**: PAT_ALLERGY (36 cols), PAT_ALLERGY_REACTION, PAT_ALLERGY_ALERT, ALLERGEN_DEF, ALLERGEN_REACTION_DEF, ALLERGEN_SEVERITY_DEF\n- **Immunizations**: PAT_IMMUNIZATION, PAT_IMMUNIZATION_EVENT, PAT_IMMUNIZATION_REGISTRY\n- **Documents & notes**: PAT_DOCUMENT (66 cols), PAT_DOCUMENT_LOB, PAT_DOCUMENT_ANNOTATION, PAT_DOCUMENT_ENTITY_REF, PAT_DOCUMENT_RECIPIENT, TRANSCRIPTION, TRANSCRIPTION_LOB, CLINICAL_NOTE_ADDENDUM, CLINICAL_NOTE_DM_STATUS, PAT_DISCHARGE_NOTE (41 cols)\n- **Billing & charges**: CHARGE_HEADER, CHARGE_LINE (29 cols), CHARGE_LINE_ICD, CHARGE_LINE_NDC, CHARGE_HEADER_SENT, CHARGE_LINE_SENT, CHARGE_LINE_SENT_ICD, CHARGE_LINE_SENT_NDC, CHARGE_COMMENT, CHARGE_ERROR, CHARGE_SOURCE, BILLABLE_ITEM, BILLING_CODE_DEF, BILLING_ORG, PAT_DOS_BILLING_SESSION\n- **Financial authorizations**: PAT_FIN_AUTH (26 cols), PAT_FIN_AUTH_BILLINGCODE, PAT_FIN_AUTH_ICD, PAT_FIN_AUTH_ORDER, PAT_FIN_AUTH_TEMPLATE_ORDER\n- **Insurance**: INSURANCE (20 cols), PATIENT_INSURANCE (20 cols)\n- **Care coordination**: PAT_CARE_PLAN, PATIENT_TRANSFER (46 cols), PATIENT_TRANSFER_PROBLEM, CCD_RECONCILIATION, CCD_MANUAL_RECONCILIATION, CQ_DOC_SEARCH_QUERY, CQ_DOC_SEARCH_RESULT, CQ_DOC_RETRIEVE_RESULT (Carequality document exchange)\n- **Appointments & scheduling**: APPOINTMENT (34 cols), APPOINTMENT_RESOURCE, APPOINTMENT_SCHEDULE, APPOINTMENT_EMCODE, NURSING_APPOINTMENT_RESOURCE\n- **Nursing care**: NURSINGCARE_IVACCESS (122 cols), NURSINGCARE_IVDEACCESS (68 cols), NURSINGCARE_PATIENTASSESS (55 cols), NURSINGCARE_PATIENTNOTE, NURSINGCARE_BILLABLE_ITEM\n- **Patient engagement**: PAT_EDUCATION_EVENT, PAT_ED_SESSION, PATIENT_MESSAGE, MAIL_MESSAGE and related\n- **Adverse events**: PATIENT_ADVERSEEVENT (27 cols), PAT_DRUGDOSE_ALERT, RXALERT\n- **Clinical trials**: CLINICAL_TRIAL_DEF (28 cols), CLINICAL_TRIAL_DEF_PREF\n- **Surveys & screenings**: PAT_SURVEY, PAT_SURVEY_ITEM, PAT_SURVEY_LINE_ITEM, PAT_SURVEY_TEMPLATE, PAT_SCREENING, PAT_SCREENING_EVENT, PAT_COVID19_SCREENING\n- **Oncology Care Model**: PAT_OCM_EPISODE (42 cols), PAT_OCM_HEADER (38 cols), PAT_OCM_MONTHLY\n- **Administrative**: PRACTICE (42 cols), PROVIDER (29 cols), LOCATION (57 cols), RESOURCES, RESOURCE_GROUP, RESOURCE_SCHEDULE\n- **E-prescribing**: ERXMESSAGEQUEUEITEM, OUTBOUND_ORDER_TX\n- **Implantable devices**: IMPLANTABLE_DEVICE (31 cols)\n- **Files & attachments**: FILE_ATTACHMENT, FILE_ATTACHMENT_LOB\n- **Other**: PATIENT_VASCULAR_ACCESS, OBGYN_HISTORY (43 cols), PAT_COGNITIVE_STATUS, PAT_DEPRESSION_STATUS, PAT_WORKFLOW_ITEM (60 cols)\n\n**Sheet 2: VBC (Value-Based Care)** — 5 tables, 60 columns. Patient eligibility, status by program, logged tasks, and attachments related to value-based care programs. No descriptions provided.\n\n**Sheet 3: Patient History** — 6 tables, 178 columns. Social determinants of health and patient-reported outcomes:\n- G2_DISTRESS_THERMOMETER (64 cols) — oncology distress screening\n- G2_SOCIALHX_INT_TRAVEL_HX — international travel history\n- G2_SOCIALHX_LIFESTYLE — lifestyle factors\n- G2_SOCIALHX_LIVING_ENV — living environment\n- G2_SOCIALHX_SUBSTANCE_USE (34 cols) — substance use history\n- G2_SOCIALHX_WORKING_ENV — working environment\nAll columns use VARCHAR2 data types with lengths. No descriptions.\n\n**Sheet 4: Ontada Health** — 2 collections, 166 fields. Uses a document/collection schema (MongoDB-style) rather than relational tables:\n- **conversation** (101 fields) — patient portal messaging with detailed conversation metadata, message threads, attachments, recipients, and routing\n- **Patient_appointment_request** (65 fields) — appointment request tracking with scheduling preferences and slot details\nFields include Data Type and Description columns, making this sheet the most descriptive after iKnowMed.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThis is a **genuinely comprehensive (b)(10) export** — one of the more thorough we've seen. The data dictionary documents what appears to be a near-complete relational database dump of the iKnowMed system, not a curated subset.\n\n**Clearly covered domains:**\n- **Patient demographics** — full coverage including race, ethnicity, language, gender identity, contacts, identifications\n- **Clinical problems/diagnoses** — problems, inferences, billing diagnosis mappings\n- **Medications** — extensive coverage: prescriptions, external medications, medication administration, dispensing, renewal requests, Rx change requests, fill notifications, drug dose alerts, medication preferences (92 columns)\n- **Orders** — the PAT_ORDER table at 182 columns is extraordinarily detailed, with associated dose, administration, inference, discontinuation, and session tables\n- **Oncology treatment** — this is where iKnowMed's specialty depth shines. Chemotherapy regimens (99 columns), cycle day management, treatment groups, treatment history, radiation treatment, surgery treatment, transfusion treatment, hospitalizations, and other treatment types are all documented\n- **Lab results** — result headers, values, attachments, with analyte and panel definitions\n- **Vitals** — daily vitals, baseline vitals, treatment vitals\n- **Allergies** — patient allergies with reactions and severity definitions\n- **Immunizations** — including registry reporting tracking\n- **Documents and notes** — patient documents with LOBs (large objects), annotations, recipients; transcriptions with LOBs; discharge notes; clinical note addenda\n- **Billing and charges** — charge headers, lines, ICD codes, NDC codes, sent charges, errors, comments — comprehensive billing record coverage\n- **Insurance** — insurance definitions and patient insurance records\n- **Financial authorizations** — prior auth tracking with billing codes, ICD codes, and orders\n- **Care coordination** — care plans, patient transfers, Carequality document exchange tracking, CCD reconciliation\n- **Nursing care** — IV access (122 columns!), de-access, patient assessments, notes, billable items\n- **Adverse events** — patient adverse events, drug dose alerts, prescription alerts\n- **Social history** — substance use, living environment, working environment, lifestyle, travel history (in Patient History sheet)\n- **Patient-reported outcomes** — distress thermometer (oncology screening), surveys, screenings\n- **Value-based care** — patient eligibility, program status, logged tasks (VBC sheet)\n- **Patient portal** — conversations, appointment requests (Ontada Health sheet)\n- **Oncology Care Model** — episode, header, and monthly tracking tables\n- **Clinical trials** — trial definitions and preferences\n- **Implantable devices** — 31 columns of device tracking\n- **Family history** — PAT_RELATIVE, PAT_RELATIVE_PROBLEM\n\n**Domains with potential gaps or ambiguity:**\n- **Cancer staging data** — While the product research describes AJCC and FIGO staging, there is no dedicated staging table. Staging information is likely embedded within PAT_PROBLEM, PAT_REGIMEN, or PAT_TREATMENT columns, but this isn't explicit from the data dictionary alone. The column descriptions in those tables could clarify this.\n- **Biomarker/molecular testing** — The product research highlights biomarker ordering and precision medicine, but there's no dedicated biomarker table. These may be represented as lab results (PAT_RESULT_HEADER/PAT_RESULT_VALUE) or within the order system, but it's not obvious.\n- **NCCN pathway compliance** — Clear Value Plus decision support data and pathway compliance tracking are product features, but it's unclear which tables store this. PAT_REGIMEN_INFERENCE and PAT_ORDER_INFERENCE might contain some of this.\n- **Clinical decision support alerts** — The ALERT table (22 cols) and PAT_CHART_ALERT may cover CDS alerts, but specifics about drug-drug interaction alerts or BSA-related alerts aren't clearly mapped.\n- **Images/imaging results** — IMAGING_DEF defines imaging types, but there's no dedicated imaging results table beyond what may be in PAT_RESULT_HEADER/VALUE or PAT_DOCUMENT.\n\n**Not missing (correctly scoped):**\n- Audit logs (not EHI) — not present, correctly excluded\n- System configuration (not EHI) — not present as patient data\n- Quality metrics aggregates (not EHI) — not present, correctly excluded\n- Provider credentialing (not EHI) — PROVIDER table has provider info but not credentialing details\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses a **proprietary pipe-delimited flat file format** — essentially a database dump with one file per table. This is an appropriate format for a (b)(10) export because:\n\n1. It captures the full relational data model, not a lossy projection into a standard like FHIR\n2. Pipe-delimited files are straightforward to parse\n3. The data dictionary provides the schema needed to interpret the files\n4. The ZIP packaging makes the export portable\n\nThis is notably **not** FHIR and is completely separate from Ontada's (g)(10) FHIR API. The FHIR API (documented elsewhere) covers 30+ US Core resource types — the (b)(10) export covers 249 entities with 5,679 fields. This is a genuine (b)(10) implementation, not a repackaged (g)(10) FHIR endpoint.\n\nThe format does have limitations:\n- **Relationships between tables are implicit** — foreign keys are present (columns like APPOINTMENT, PATIENT, PRACTICE reference IDs) but there's no explicit relationship documentation or ERD\n- **No sample data** — there are no example export files to demonstrate the actual format\n- **Value sets are undocumented** — coded fields (many columns appear to use numeric codes) don't have their value set mappings documented in the data dictionary\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Strengths:**\n- The data dictionary is substantial — 249 entities covering what appears to be the full database schema\n- The main iKnowMed sheet includes both table-level and column-level descriptions\n- Data types and lengths are consistently documented\n- The column descriptions often include Java class type annotations (e.g., \"Appointment appointment; (optional)\") which reveal the object model\n\n**Weaknesses:**\n- **Minimal export instructions** — the web page provides only a brief paragraph about the export being a ZIP with pipe-delimited files. There are no step-by-step instructions for how a user actually triggers the export\n- **No sample data** — no example export files are provided\n- **No relationship documentation** — no entity-relationship diagram or foreign key documentation. A developer would need to reverse-engineer table relationships from column names\n- **Inconsistent descriptions** — the VBC and Patient History sheets lack column descriptions entirely. The Ontada Health sheet has descriptions but in a different schema format\n- **No value set documentation** — columns that contain coded values (e.g., status codes, type codes) don't document what the valid codes are or what they mean\n- **Column descriptions are terse** — many descriptions are just the Java class name (e.g., \"PatAllergy\") which tells you the object model class but not the business meaning\n\nA developer could construct a reasonable data import from this documentation, but would struggle with:\n- Understanding which codes mean what in coded fields\n- Knowing the exact relationships between tables\n- Understanding the actual file format details (encoding, header rows, null representation, escaping rules for pipe characters in data)\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n**Granularity**: Field-level documentation with column names, data types, and lengths for all 5,679 fields. Column descriptions present for the iKnowMed sheet (~5,275 columns) but absent for VBC and Patient History sheets.\n\n**Data types**: Consistently documented across sheets — NUMBER, VARCHAR2, DATE, CLOB, TIMESTAMP for relational sheets; String, Boolean, int, UUID, Array for Ontada Health collections.\n\n**Cardinality**: Not explicitly documented, but the column descriptions often include \"(optional)\" annotations from the Java model.\n\n**Relationships**: Not documented. Foreign keys must be inferred from column naming conventions (e.g., PATIENT column in most tables likely references PATIENT.ID).\n\n**Value sets**: Not documented. This is the single biggest gap — without knowing what the coded values mean, many fields are opaque.\n\n**Versioning**: No version number or change history on the data dictionary. The XLSX has no metadata about when it was last updated.\n\n## Overall Assessment\n\nOntada's (b)(10) EHI export documentation is **above average** for the industry. The key strengths are:\n\n1. **This is a real (b)(10) export**, not a repackaged FHIR API. The 249-table, 5,679-field data dictionary describes a comprehensive database dump that goes far beyond USCDI/US Core data classes.\n\n2. **The oncology specialty data is well represented.** Chemotherapy regimens, cycle day management, treatment history, radiation/surgery/transfusion treatments, adverse events, nursing care (including detailed IV access documentation), distress screening, and Oncology Care Model tracking are all present. This reflects the product's deep oncology specialization.\n\n3. **Billing data is included.** The CHARGE_* tables, financial authorization tables, insurance tables, and billing session tables demonstrate coverage of the billing domain — a common gap in other vendors' exports.\n\n4. **Patient portal and VBC data are included.** Separate sheets for the Ontada Health patient portal (conversations, appointment requests) and Value-Based Care program data show these subsystems are exported.\n\nThe documentation falls short in:\n1. **Lack of export procedure documentation** — no instructions for how to actually perform the export\n2. **Missing value set definitions** — coded fields are documented structurally but not semantically\n3. **No relationship documentation** — the relational model must be reverse-engineered\n4. **No sample data or format specification** — the exact pipe-delimited format details (encoding, escaping, headers) are undocumented\n5. **Minimal web page** — the entire export documentation is essentially one paragraph plus one XLSX file\n\nDespite these gaps, the breadth of data documented in the data dictionary is impressive. A recipient of this export would have a nearly complete dump of the oncology EHR's database, covering clinical, billing, nursing, patient engagement, and specialty oncology data.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.ontada.com/point-of-care-solutions/ehi/\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (curl works fine)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link (one redirect, then a single page with one download link)\n- Anti-bot issues: Cloudflare and Imperva CDN present but did not block requests with standard User-Agent header\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The registered URL (`/Providers-Solutions/EHI/`) 301-redirects to `/point-of-care-solutions/ehi/` — appears to be a site reorganization. The redirect works cleanly.\n- No obstacles encountered. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01AA4qVLnVNoznmYbEh8hVx4","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: /home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/mckesson-specialty-health-technology-products-llc-ontada--iknowmed-generation-2/ehi-export-report.md"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"bf663c9b-80e5-4ddc-b9b4-2d3543e1f5f6","uuid":"33e3349f-4ae7-45f0-bd04-e47392ffd54b","tool_use_result":{"type":"create","filePath":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/mckesson-specialty-health-technology-products-llc-ontada--iknowmed-generation-2/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# McKesson Specialty Health Technology Products LLC (Ontada) — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://www.ontada.com/Providers-Solutions/EHI/\n- Final URL (after redirect): https://www.ontada.com/point-of-care-solutions/ehi/\n- CHPL ID: 9580 (15.04.04.2920.iKno.30.01.1.180508)\n- Product: iKnowMed Generation 2, Version 3\n- Certification date: 2018-05-08\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Initial probe** — HTTP HEAD with curl:\n   ```\n   curl -sI -L \"https://www.ontada.com/Providers-Solutions/EHI/\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n   ```\n   Result: 301 redirect from `/Providers-Solutions/EHI/` to `/point-of-care-solutions/ehi/`, then 200 OK with `text/html` content type. Site is behind Cloudflare and Imperva CDN.\n\n2. **Fetched the page** — 72KB HTML page titled \"iKnowMed® EHI Export Capabilities\". The page is a simple single-page document (not an SPA) with:\n   - A brief description of the EHI export format\n   - A link to the (b)(10) Data Dictionary (XLSX)\n   - A list of factors that affect export content variability\n   - No additional sub-pages, accordions, or hidden sections\n\n3. **Found downloadable file** — searched HTML for file links:\n   ```\n   grep -oiE 'href=\"[^\"]*\\.(pdf|zip|xlsx|xls|csv|json)' page.html\n   ```\n   Found one file: `/siteassets/documents/b10_data_dictionary.xlsx`\n\n4. **Downloaded the data dictionary**:\n   ```\n   curl -sL \"https://www.ontada.com/siteassets/documents/b10_data_dictionary.xlsx\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o b10_data_dictionary.xlsx\n   ```\n   Confirmed: `file` reports \"Microsoft Excel 2007+\", 240KB.\n\n5. **Took a full-page screenshot** of the EHI page in Chrome for visual documentation.\n\n6. **No additional documentation found.** The page contains only the description and the single data dictionary download. There are no links to export format specifications, API docs, sample data, schema files, or user guides beyond what is on the page. The two external links on the page (to healthit.gov and the ONC certification criteria) are standard regulatory references, not vendor-specific documentation.\n\n## What Was Found\n\n### Export Format\n\nThe EHI export from iKnowMed Generation 2 produces a **ZIP file containing pipe-delimited (|) flat files** — one file per table/entity in the export. This is a proprietary database dump format, not a standard like FHIR or C-CDA. The page explicitly states this satisfies §170.315(b)(10).\n\nThe page notes that export content varies by organization based on:\n- Which iKnowMed features are in use\n- Configuration decisions made by the healthcare organization\n- The organization's clinical utilization of iKnowMed\n- The documentation in place at the healthcare organization\n\n### Data Dictionary (b10_data_dictionary.xlsx)\n\nThe data dictionary is a substantial Excel workbook with **4 sheets, 249 entities, and 5,679 field definitions**:\n\n**Sheet 1: iKnowMed** — 236 tables, 5,275 columns. This is the core EHR database schema and constitutes the vast majority of the export. Each row provides: TABLE_NAME, COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE, DATA_LENGTH, TABLE_DESC, and COLUMN_DESC. The descriptions are brief (typically just the Java class name) but present for most tables. Column descriptions are more substantive, often including the Java field type and optional/required annotations.\n\nKey table groups in the iKnowMed sheet:\n- **Patient demographics**: PATIENT (57 cols), PATIENT_CONTACT, PATIENT_IDENTIFICATION, PAT_RACE, PAT_ETHNICITY, PAT_LANGUAGE, PAT_GENDER_IDENTITY\n- **Clinical problems & diagnoses**: PAT_PROBLEM (36 cols), PAT_PROBLEM_INFERENCE, PROBLEM_DEF, BILLING_DIAG_DEF\n- **Medications & prescribing**: MEDICATION (53 cols), PATIENT_MEDICATION, PRESCRIPTION (35 cols), MEDICATION_PREFERENCE (92 cols), DISPENSABLE (35 cols), NEWDRUGRXTEMPLATE, RXRENEWALREQUEST, RX_CHANGE_REQUEST, RX_FILL_NOTIFICATION\n- **Orders & administration**: PAT_ORDER (182 cols — the largest table), PAT_ORDER_DOSE (75 cols), PAT_ORDER_ADMINISTRATION, PAT_ORDER_SESSION, PAT_ORDER_GROUP, PAT_ORDER_DISCONTINUATION, PAT_ORDER_INFERENCE\n- **Treatment regimens (oncology-specific)**: PAT_REGIMEN (99 cols), PAT_REGIMEN_CYCLE_DAYS, PAT_REGIMEN_INFERENCE, PAT_REGIMEN_SEQUENCE, PAT_REGIMEN_TREATMENT_GROUP, REGIMEN_DEF (41 cols), PAT_CHEMO_TREATMENT (34 cols), DATE_CYCLE_DAY, CYCLE_DAY_DELAY, CYCLE_DAY_MOVE\n- **Other oncology treatments**: PATIENT_RADIATION_TREATMENT (29 cols), PATIENT_SURGERY_TREATMENT, PAT_HOSPITAL_TREATMENT, PAT_OTHER_TREATMENT, PAT_PROCEDURE_TREATMENT, PAT_TRANSFUSN_TREATMENT, PAT_TREATMENT (49 cols), PAT_TREATMENT_HISTORY (54 cols)\n- **Lab results**: PAT_RESULT_HEADER (53 cols), PAT_RESULT_VALUE (41 cols), PAT_RESULT_ATTACHMENT, LAB_ANALYTE_DEF, LAB_PANEL_DEF, EXTERNAL_RESULT_PANEL_DEF, EXTERNAL_RESULT_VALUE_DEF\n- **Vitals & observations**: DAILY_VITALS, BASELINE_VITAL (28 cols), TREATMENT_VITAL (22 cols), TREATMENT_VITAL_SET, PAT_PERFORMANCE_STATUS, PATIENT_SMOKING_STATUS\n- **Allergies**: PAT_ALLERGY (36 cols), PAT_ALLERGY_REACTION, PAT_ALLERGY_ALERT, ALLERGEN_DEF, ALLERGEN_REACTION_DEF, ALLERGEN_SEVERITY_DEF\n- **Immunizations**: PAT_IMMUNIZATION, PAT_IMMUNIZATION_EVENT, PAT_IMMUNIZATION_REGISTRY\n- **Documents & notes**: PAT_DOCUMENT (66 cols), PAT_DOCUMENT_LOB, PAT_DOCUMENT_ANNOTATION, PAT_DOCUMENT_ENTITY_REF, PAT_DOCUMENT_RECIPIENT, TRANSCRIPTION, TRANSCRIPTION_LOB, CLINICAL_NOTE_ADDENDUM, CLINICAL_NOTE_DM_STATUS, PAT_DISCHARGE_NOTE (41 cols)\n- **Billing & charges**: CHARGE_HEADER, CHARGE_LINE (29 cols), CHARGE_LINE_ICD, CHARGE_LINE_NDC, CHARGE_HEADER_SENT, CHARGE_LINE_SENT, CHARGE_LINE_SENT_ICD, CHARGE_LINE_SENT_NDC, CHARGE_COMMENT, CHARGE_ERROR, CHARGE_SOURCE, BILLABLE_ITEM, BILLING_CODE_DEF, BILLING_ORG, PAT_DOS_BILLING_SESSION\n- **Financial authorizations**: PAT_FIN_AUTH (26 cols), PAT_FIN_AUTH_BILLINGCODE, PAT_FIN_AUTH_ICD, PAT_FIN_AUTH_ORDER, PAT_FIN_AUTH_TEMPLATE_ORDER\n- **Insurance**: INSURANCE (20 cols), PATIENT_INSURANCE (20 cols)\n- **Care coordination**: PAT_CARE_PLAN, PATIENT_TRANSFER (46 cols), PATIENT_TRANSFER_PROBLEM, CCD_RECONCILIATION, CCD_MANUAL_RECONCILIATION, CQ_DOC_SEARCH_QUERY, CQ_DOC_SEARCH_RESULT, CQ_DOC_RETRIEVE_RESULT (Carequality document exchange)\n- **Appointments & scheduling**: APPOINTMENT (34 cols), APPOINTMENT_RESOURCE, APPOINTMENT_SCHEDULE, APPOINTMENT_EMCODE, NURSING_APPOINTMENT_RESOURCE\n- **Nursing care**: NURSINGCARE_IVACCESS (122 cols), NURSINGCARE_IVDEACCESS (68 cols), NURSINGCARE_PATIENTASSESS (55 cols), NURSINGCARE_PATIENTNOTE, NURSINGCARE_BILLABLE_ITEM\n- **Patient engagement**: PAT_EDUCATION_EVENT, PAT_ED_SESSION, PATIENT_MESSAGE, MAIL_MESSAGE and related\n- **Adverse events**: PATIENT_ADVERSEEVENT (27 cols), PAT_DRUGDOSE_ALERT, RXALERT\n- **Clinical trials**: CLINICAL_TRIAL_DEF (28 cols), CLINICAL_TRIAL_DEF_PREF\n- **Surveys & screenings**: PAT_SURVEY, PAT_SURVEY_ITEM, PAT_SURVEY_LINE_ITEM, PAT_SURVEY_TEMPLATE, PAT_SCREENING, PAT_SCREENING_EVENT, PAT_COVID19_SCREENING\n- **Oncology Care Model**: PAT_OCM_EPISODE (42 cols), PAT_OCM_HEADER (38 cols), PAT_OCM_MONTHLY\n- **Administrative**: PRACTICE (42 cols), PROVIDER (29 cols), LOCATION (57 cols), RESOURCES, RESOURCE_GROUP, RESOURCE_SCHEDULE\n- **E-prescribing**: ERXMESSAGEQUEUEITEM, OUTBOUND_ORDER_TX\n- **Implantable devices**: IMPLANTABLE_DEVICE (31 cols)\n- **Files & attachments**: FILE_ATTACHMENT, FILE_ATTACHMENT_LOB\n- **Other**: PATIENT_VASCULAR_ACCESS, OBGYN_HISTORY (43 cols), PAT_COGNITIVE_STATUS, PAT_DEPRESSION_STATUS, PAT_WORKFLOW_ITEM (60 cols)\n\n**Sheet 2: VBC (Value-Based Care)** — 5 tables, 60 columns. Patient eligibility, status by program, logged tasks, and attachments related to value-based care programs. No descriptions provided.\n\n**Sheet 3: Patient History** — 6 tables, 178 columns. Social determinants of health and patient-reported outcomes:\n- G2_DISTRESS_THERMOMETER (64 cols) — oncology distress screening\n- G2_SOCIALHX_INT_TRAVEL_HX — international travel history\n- G2_SOCIALHX_LIFESTYLE — lifestyle factors\n- G2_SOCIALHX_LIVING_ENV — living environment\n- G2_SOCIALHX_SUBSTANCE_USE (34 cols) — substance use history\n- G2_SOCIALHX_WORKING_ENV — working environment\nAll columns use VARCHAR2 data types with lengths. No descriptions.\n\n**Sheet 4: Ontada Health** — 2 collections, 166 fields. Uses a document/collection schema (MongoDB-style) rather than relational tables:\n- **conversation** (101 fields) — patient portal messaging with detailed conversation metadata, message threads, attachments, recipients, and routing\n- **Patient_appointment_request** (65 fields) — appointment request tracking with scheduling preferences and slot details\nFields include Data Type and Description columns, making this sheet the most descriptive after iKnowMed.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThis is a **genuinely comprehensive (b)(10) export** — one of the more thorough we've seen. The data dictionary documents what appears to be a near-complete relational database dump of the iKnowMed system, not a curated subset.\n\n**Clearly covered domains:**\n- **Patient demographics** — full coverage including race, ethnicity, language, gender identity, contacts, identifications\n- **Clinical problems/diagnoses** — problems, inferences, billing diagnosis mappings\n- **Medications** — extensive coverage: prescriptions, external medications, medication administration, dispensing, renewal requests, Rx change requests, fill notifications, drug dose alerts, medication preferences (92 columns)\n- **Orders** — the PAT_ORDER table at 182 columns is extraordinarily detailed, with associated dose, administration, inference, discontinuation, and session tables\n- **Oncology treatment** — this is where iKnowMed's specialty depth shines. Chemotherapy regimens (99 columns), cycle day management, treatment groups, treatment history, radiation treatment, surgery treatment, transfusion treatment, hospitalizations, and other treatment types are all documented\n- **Lab results** — result headers, values, attachments, with analyte and panel definitions\n- **Vitals** — daily vitals, baseline vitals, treatment vitals\n- **Allergies** — patient allergies with reactions and severity definitions\n- **Immunizations** — including registry reporting tracking\n- **Documents and notes** — patient documents with LOBs (large objects), annotations, recipients; transcriptions with LOBs; discharge notes; clinical note addenda\n- **Billing and charges** — charge headers, lines, ICD codes, NDC codes, sent charges, errors, comments — comprehensive billing record coverage\n- **Insurance** — insurance definitions and patient insurance records\n- **Financial authorizations** — prior auth tracking with billing codes, ICD codes, and orders\n- **Care coordination** — care plans, patient transfers, Carequality document exchange tracking, CCD reconciliation\n- **Nursing care** — IV access (122 columns!), de-access, patient assessments, notes, billable items\n- **Adverse events** — patient adverse events, drug dose alerts, prescription alerts\n- **Social history** — substance use, living environment, working environment, lifestyle, travel history (in Patient History sheet)\n- **Patient-reported outcomes** — distress thermometer (oncology screening), surveys, screenings\n- **Value-based care** — patient eligibility, program status, logged tasks (VBC sheet)\n- **Patient portal** — conversations, appointment requests (Ontada Health sheet)\n- **Oncology Care Model** — episode, header, and monthly tracking tables\n- **Clinical trials** — trial definitions and preferences\n- **Implantable devices** — 31 columns of device tracking\n- **Family history** — PAT_RELATIVE, PAT_RELATIVE_PROBLEM\n\n**Domains with potential gaps or ambiguity:**\n- **Cancer staging data** — While the product research describes AJCC and FIGO staging, there is no dedicated staging table. Staging information is likely embedded within PAT_PROBLEM, PAT_REGIMEN, or PAT_TREATMENT columns, but this isn't explicit from the data dictionary alone. The column descriptions in those tables could clarify this.\n- **Biomarker/molecular testing** — The product research highlights biomarker ordering and precision medicine, but there's no dedicated biomarker table. These may be represented as lab results (PAT_RESULT_HEADER/PAT_RESULT_VALUE) or within the order system, but it's not obvious.\n- **NCCN pathway compliance** — Clear Value Plus decision support data and pathway compliance tracking are product features, but it's unclear which tables store this. PAT_REGIMEN_INFERENCE and PAT_ORDER_INFERENCE might contain some of this.\n- **Clinical decision support alerts** — The ALERT table (22 cols) and PAT_CHART_ALERT may cover CDS alerts, but specifics about drug-drug interaction alerts or BSA-related alerts aren't clearly mapped.\n- **Images/imaging results** — IMAGING_DEF defines imaging types, but there's no dedicated imaging results table beyond what may be in PAT_RESULT_HEADER/VALUE or PAT_DOCUMENT.\n\n**Not missing (correctly scoped):**\n- Audit logs (not EHI) — not present, correctly excluded\n- System configuration (not EHI) — not present as patient data\n- Quality metrics aggregates (not EHI) — not present, correctly excluded\n- Provider credentialing (not EHI) — PROVIDER table has provider info but not credentialing details\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses a **proprietary pipe-delimited flat file format** — essentially a database dump with one file per table. This is an appropriate format for a (b)(10) export because:\n\n1. It captures the full relational data model, not a lossy projection into a standard like FHIR\n2. Pipe-delimited files are straightforward to parse\n3. The data dictionary provides the schema needed to interpret the files\n4. The ZIP packaging makes the export portable\n\nThis is notably **not** FHIR and is completely separate from Ontada's (g)(10) FHIR API. The FHIR API (documented elsewhere) covers 30+ US Core resource types — the (b)(10) export covers 249 entities with 5,679 fields. This is a genuine (b)(10) implementation, not a repackaged (g)(10) FHIR endpoint.\n\nThe format does have limitations:\n- **Relationships between tables are implicit** — foreign keys are present (columns like APPOINTMENT, PATIENT, PRACTICE reference IDs) but there's no explicit relationship documentation or ERD\n- **No sample data** — there are no example export files to demonstrate the actual format\n- **Value sets are undocumented** — coded fields (many columns appear to use numeric codes) don't have their value set mappings documented in the data dictionary\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Strengths:**\n- The data dictionary is substantial — 249 entities covering what appears to be the full database schema\n- The main iKnowMed sheet includes both table-level and column-level descriptions\n- Data types and lengths are consistently documented\n- The column descriptions often include Java class type annotations (e.g., \"Appointment appointment; (optional)\") which reveal the object model\n\n**Weaknesses:**\n- **Minimal export instructions** — the web page provides only a brief paragraph about the export being a ZIP with pipe-delimited files. There are no step-by-step instructions for how a user actually triggers the export\n- **No sample data** — no example export files are provided\n- **No relationship documentation** — no entity-relationship diagram or foreign key documentation. A developer would need to reverse-engineer table relationships from column names\n- **Inconsistent descriptions** — the VBC and Patient History sheets lack column descriptions entirely. The Ontada Health sheet has descriptions but in a different schema format\n- **No value set documentation** — columns that contain coded values (e.g., status codes, type codes) don't document what the valid codes are or what they mean\n- **Column descriptions are terse** — many descriptions are just the Java class name (e.g., \"PatAllergy\") which tells you the object model class but not the business meaning\n\nA developer could construct a reasonable data import from this documentation, but would struggle with:\n- Understanding which codes mean what in coded fields\n- Knowing the exact relationships between tables\n- Understanding the actual file format details (encoding, header rows, null representation, escaping rules for pipe characters in data)\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n**Granularity**: Field-level documentation with column names, data types, and lengths for all 5,679 fields. Column descriptions present for the iKnowMed sheet (~5,275 columns) but absent for VBC and Patient History sheets.\n\n**Data types**: Consistently documented across sheets — NUMBER, VARCHAR2, DATE, CLOB, TIMESTAMP for relational sheets; String, Boolean, int, UUID, Array for Ontada Health collections.\n\n**Cardinality**: Not explicitly documented, but the column descriptions often include \"(optional)\" annotations from the Java model.\n\n**Relationships**: Not documented. Foreign keys must be inferred from column naming conventions (e.g., PATIENT column in most tables likely references PATIENT.ID).\n\n**Value sets**: Not documented. This is the single biggest gap — without knowing what the coded values mean, many fields are opaque.\n\n**Versioning**: No version number or change history on the data dictionary. The XLSX has no metadata about when it was last updated.\n\n## Overall Assessment\n\nOntada's (b)(10) EHI export documentation is **above average** for the industry. The key strengths are:\n\n1. **This is a real (b)(10) export**, not a repackaged FHIR API. The 249-table, 5,679-field data dictionary describes a comprehensive database dump that goes far beyond USCDI/US Core data classes.\n\n2. **The oncology specialty data is well represented.** Chemotherapy regimens, cycle day management, treatment history, radiation/surgery/transfusion treatments, adverse events, nursing care (including detailed IV access documentation), distress screening, and Oncology Care Model tracking are all present. This reflects the product's deep oncology specialization.\n\n3. **Billing data is included.** The CHARGE_* tables, financial authorization tables, insurance tables, and billing session tables demonstrate coverage of the billing domain — a common gap in other vendors' exports.\n\n4. **Patient portal and VBC data are included.** Separate sheets for the Ontada Health patient portal (conversations, appointment requests) and Value-Based Care program data show these subsystems are exported.\n\nThe documentation falls short in:\n1. **Lack of export procedure documentation** — no instructions for how to actually perform the export\n2. **Missing value set definitions** — coded fields are documented structurally but not semantically\n3. **No relationship documentation** — the relational model must be reverse-engineered\n4. **No sample data or format specification** — the exact pipe-delimited format details (encoding, escaping, headers) are undocumented\n5. **Minimal web page** — the entire export documentation is essentially one paragraph plus one XLSX file\n\nDespite these gaps, the breadth of data documented in the data dictionary is impressive. A recipient of this export would have a nearly complete dump of the oncology EHR's database, covering clinical, billing, nursing, patient engagement, and specialty oncology data.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.ontada.com/point-of-care-solutions/ehi/\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (curl works fine)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link (one redirect, then a single page with one download link)\n- Anti-bot issues: Cloudflare and Imperva CDN present but did not block requests with standard User-Agent header\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The registered URL (`/Providers-Solutions/EHI/`) 301-redirects to `/point-of-care-solutions/ehi/` — appears to be a site reorganization. The redirect works cleanly.\n- No obstacles encountered. The page loaded immediately, the XLSX downloaded without issues, and no authentication was required.\n- `pip` was not available in the environment for `openpyxl`, but `bun` with the `xlsx` npm package worked as an alternative for parsing the Excel file.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}
